title: Python parity: warp.py effective grid, markup snapping, shared parity fixtures
description:
## Intent
Python parity: analysis and markup respect your grid.

## Scope
- New `analysis/apricity_analyze/warp.py`: `effective_grid(manifest) -> list[{seconds, beat}]` and `check_user_warp_markers(manifest) -> list[str]` (same rules and messages as Rust).
- `markup.py`: bar lines for sections and loops from `effective_grid`; never creates or removes markers named `warp` (they are user markers; the existing keep-non-ML rule already keeps them; add an assertion test).
- `analyze.py`: re-analysis keeps annotations (already) — add the test.
- `server.py` `PUT /api/annotations`: runs `check_user_warp_markers` (until apricitus-8cecf2 retires it).
- **Parity**: one fixture set `crates/apricity-score/tests/fixtures/warp_parity/*.json` (manifest + expected grid or expected errors) read by `crates/apricity-score/tests/warp_parity.rs` and `analysis/tests/test_warp.py`, like `rank_parity.rs`.

## Verify
`PYTHONPATH=analysis analysis/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q analysis/tests/test_warp.py analysis/tests/test_markup.py analysis/tests/test_server.py` and `safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-score --test warp_parity`.

Commit: `feat(<this id>): analysis and markup use warp markers of yours`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
